newsitem.title: USA: 4 killed, 2 wounded in Detroit shooting rampage.
newsitem.headline: 4 killed, 2 wounded in Detroit shooting rampage.

text.p: A gunman dressed in camouflage killed two bank employees and a hostage on Tuesday during an apparent attempted robbery before police shot him dead in a hail of bullets.
The gunman, armed with a shotgun, also wounded at least two others, police said, including a man on the street shot in the face at random before the gunman entered the bank.

Deputy Detroit Police Chief Benny Napoleon said it was unclear whether the gunman intended to rob the bank. The "obviously very troubled young man" in his early 20s shouted religious passages and ordered people inside the bank to recite the Lord's Prayer, he said.
Inside the bank, the gunman shot and killed two employees and wounded another woman in the chin after police, notified when a silent alarm was tripped, surrounded the bank.
The gunman left the bank and fled into an alley, taking with him as hostage a man who was using an automatic teller machine.
Napoleon said the gunman, holding the hostage by the neck, fired at police several times, but added that police did not return fire because they did not want to injure the hostage.

"He then shot, fatally wounded, the hostage that he had taken at the automatic teller machine, he shot him in the head," Napoleon told reporters. "At that point in time, the police officers fatally wounded the perpetrator."
A tow truck driver who witnessed the shooting told WWJ Radio that the gunman "grabbed the guy around the neck, and put the gun to his head and the police just started loading up on him."

At St. John's Hospital and Medical Centre in Detroit, the 23-year-old man shot in the face was listed in serious condition, and a 38-year-old woman shot inside the bank was listed in fair condition, according to a spokeswoman.
A pregnant woman in the bank who was not injured also apparently was taken to a hospital for observation.
